memory_candidates.content: install-extension.sh's symlink-creation sites hardcode a relative path string (rel_path="../<depth>/extensions/$EXT_NAME/...") rather than deriving it from the actual filesystem depth. Any future relocation of the extension source-store root will silently break every existing symlink it created, and the script cannot self-repair: install_commands/install_skills only warn on a mismatched existing symlink target, and install_agents does not validate an existing symlink's target at all. Repair requires an explicit delete-then-recreate (delete stale symlinks, then re-run install-extension.sh for the affected extension) -- simply fixing the hardcoded path and re-running the installer over an already-broken symlink is a no-op, because the install functions treat 'symlink already exists' (even dangling) as 'nothing to do'.

When adding a multi-severity check to a shell-based lint/gate script that must land advisory-first and later promote to blocking (a common two-phase rollout pattern for new gate rules), route all new checks through one shared reporter function controlled by a single mode variable (e.g. orphan_report() gated by ORPHAN_GATE_MODE="advisory"|"hard"), rather than writing separate info/fail branches per check. The later promotion becomes a single default-value flip instead of N separate edits, and both severities stay trivially testable via an env-var override without touching the checked-in default.

A merge-into-shared-JSON step (here: install-extension.sh's merge_index_entries, which jq-merges an extension's index-entries.json fragment into the deployed context/index.json) can transiently drop unrelated pre-existing entries as a side effect, even when the merge's own logic appears correct in isolated replica testing. Before trusting any such merge step's output, diff the full set of entry keys/paths before vs after (not just spot-checking the newly-added entries) to catch silent unrelated drops.
